records.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
records.response_truth:
Three hours. We have three hours and apparently everyone's decided that means we're done.

I'm not going to make anyone do anything, but I also don't really want to leave this place looking like this. Not for any sentimental reason — I just think there's something to be said for not leaving a mess behind, even one that technically doesn't belong to us anymore.

I'm going to start breaking down the things that should come down. If anyone wants to help, I'll take it. If not, I'll do what I can.

records.response_pred:

*clears throat*

That was weirdly long and awkward to say out loud. Sorry. Let me rephrase that.

We need to talk about what happens when there's a lull. Not just after the excitement of rescue, but every other time. Because I think we're as well organized as we can be right now, but we lose momentum fast when there's nothing to react to. And I don't think that's a good long-term plan.

I have suggestions, but I also think we need an actual discussion about this, and I'm not sure when the last time was that we talked about group dynamics. So — let's do that. Right now. Not in a minute, not after lunch, not later today. Right now, before it gets dark, because I think we're in danger of losing some of the cohesion we've built up, and that's not okay.

records.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.
records.response_pred:

*waits for answer*

I didn't dream of my family or my room or my street or any of the stuff you're probably thinking of. records.response_truth:

But here's the thing. We all had emergencies. Every single day of the last three days was an emergency in some form, and the plan we all agreed to was that we'd face those together, with the same information and the same resources. When you took things out of that shared pool, even with good intentions, you made a decision for all of us without telling us. And that's the part that was hard. Not the fear — the fear I completely understand. The not telling us.

I'm not angry. I think I was, a little, in the middle of it. But we're three hours from rescue and you just laid it all out in front of everyone, and that took something.

I just — I needed to say that directly, because I said I would and I meant it. Now it's said. We're good.

Help me get this shelter down?
records.response_pred:
**sighs**

I keep things for emergencies too. This whole thing is a reminder that emergencies can feel a lot like life itself, sometimes. That it's possible to get through a lot without ever really thinking about what you'd do if you were suddenly cut off from everything you were counting on.

So — I'm not sure what I would've done without the rationing plan. But I'm pretty sure that it's something I wouldn't have thought of before I was in this camp. And that's okay. I mean, it doesn't make it okay to not have thought of it, exactly, but it's not like I can change that now, right?

So. I don't know what I would've done without that bottle and those crackers. But I know I would've done something, and I think that's probably the important part, for me.

For you, though — I don't know. I don't know what you would've done, or what you would've had. And I don't think that's something I'm going to figure out, exactly, in this moment. But I do think it matters. And I think it's probably worth thinking about.

records.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?

None. They didn't serve a practical purpose.
